questions.question: Which of the following metals will NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas?

questions.question: When a person suffers from indigestion due to excess acid in the stomach, they often consume an antacid. This process is an example of which type of chemical reaction?

options.explanation: An oxidation reaction involves the loss of electrons, which is not relevant to the reaction between an antacid and stomach acid.

A precipitation reaction involves the formation of a solid from a solution, which is not relevant to the reaction between an antacid and stomach acid.

questions.explanation: Antacids contain bases (like magnesium hydroxide or aluminium hydroxide) which react with the excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach to form salt and water, thereby neutralizing the acid and relieving indigestion.

questions.question: A solution has a hydroxide ion concentration [OH⁻] of 1 x 10⁻³ mol/L. What is its pH value?

options.explanation: This pH value is acidic, not basic.
This pH value corresponds to the given [OH⁻] concentration.
This pH value is neutral, not basic.
This pH value is strongly acidic, not basic.

questions.explanation: Given [OH⁻] = 1 x 10⁻³ mol/L, pOH = -log[OH⁻] = -log(1 x 10⁻³) = 3. For aqueous solutions at 25°C, pH + pOH = 14. So, pH = 14 - pOH = 14 - 3 = 11.
